text.p: German drugs group Schering AG on Friday delighted investors by confirming it would raise its 1996 dividend by nearly 30 percent to two marks a share, letting them participate in stronger than expected profits.
Schering's share price rose 55 pfennigs to 163 marks in bourse trade and climbed to 163.90 in after-hours trading after the group's supervisory board approved the decision.

Chief financial officer Klaus Pohle had already promised the payout would climb to two marks in November, as the group relished a 66 percent jump in nine-month profits, leaving behind a difficult previous year.

Schering, the world's largest manufacturer of oral contraceptives, then went on to beat even its own forecasts for the full year, posting a 46 percent jump in consolidated earnings to a record 362 million marks ($212.4 million).
The group's net profit climbed nine percent to 211 million marks, Schering said, adding that 74 million marks were being put into revenue reserves.
Group sales climbed 13 percent to 5.27 billion marks.
The increase was largely fuelled by acquisitions and strong sales of Schering's own products like multiple-sclerosis drug Betaferon, which was launched in Europe in 1996.

Another huge bonus for Schering were improved currency relationships which only one year earlier wreaked havoc on the drugmaker, whose bulks costs are incurred in Germany but whose biggest single market is the United States Schering exports over 85 percent of its products.

Analysts said that when viewed in comparison with 1995, considered a true disaster for the Berlin-based group, 1996 was a sign that the company was still on track and could achieve still stronger performances.

In 1995 Schering results were dented not only by the very weak dollar but also by the recall of its promising Isovist-280 x-ray drug which cost the company 193 million marks and health authority warnings that one of Schering's contraceptive pills could raise the risks of thrombosis.
"We see clear growth with the share price having room to move towards the 200 mark level in several years," Ludger Mues, analyst at WestLB in Duesseldorf said.
However Pohle cautioned that profits would grow at a single-digit level this year with sales likely to hit 5.9 million marks this year.

Pohle explained that Schering will face costs of some 70 million marks next year for its acquisitions of Leiras and Jenapharm, and analysts added that the group may fear a new bout of currency turmoil or softer volume sales.
Schering will offer more details about its 1996 results at a news conference in Berlin on Wednesday.
